provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Living things grow
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify living things.
The pupils should be able to order growth stages.
Introduction:
We see babies grow into adults.
Plants and animals also grow.
Content:
Living things change size over time.
A baby becomes a big adult person.
A seed grows into a tall tree.
A chick becomes a big chicken.
Class activity:
Let us play the growth game.
Line up cards from baby to adult.
Evaluation questions:
What do living things do?
Show me a baby picture.
Show me an adult picture.
Summary:
All living things grow and change.
They start small and become big.

topics.title: Plant life cycle
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list plant stages.
The pupils should be able to order the cycle.
Introduction:
We see plants around us.
Plants start from seeds.
Content:
A plant has a life cycle.
First there is a seed in the soil.
Then a sprout comes out.
The sprout grows into a plant.
The plant makes flowers.
Flowers make fruits with seeds.
Class activity:
Let us arrange the plant cycle cards.
Start with seed and end with fruit.
Evaluation questions:
What comes after a seed?
What does a flower make?
Show me the plant cycle.
Summary:
Plants grow in stages from seed to fruit.

topics.title: Butterfly life cycle
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name butterfly stages.
The pupils should be able to act the cycle.
Introduction:
Butterflies are beautiful insects.
They change in four stages.
Content:
A butterfly starts as an egg.
The egg becomes a caterpillar.
The caterpillar makes a pupa.
The pupa opens and a butterfly comes out.
This is called metamorphosis.
Class activity:
Let us be butterflies.
We will curl up like eggs.
Then crawl like caterpillars.
Then sleep like pupas.
Then fly like butterflies.
Evaluation questions:
What comes after the egg?
What is a pupa?
Show me how a butterfly flies.
Summary:
Butterflies change in four amazing stages.

topics.title: Habitats
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify animal habitats.
The pupils should be able to match animals to homes.
Introduction:
Animals live in different places.
These places are called habitats.
Content:
A habitat is where an animal lives.
Fish live in water.
Birds live in trees.
Goats live on land.
Some animals live in holes.
Class activity:
Let us play match the game.
Put fish in water picture.
Put bird in tree picture.
Evaluation questions:
Where does a fish live?
Where does a bird build its nest?
Show me a land animal.
Summary:
Animals have special places they call home.

topics.title: Food chains start
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain simple food chains.
The pupils should be able to identify producers.
Introduction:
All living things need food.
Food chains show who eats what.
Content:
A food chain starts with a plant.
The plant makes its own food.
An animal eats the plant.
Another animal eats that animal.
For example grass feeds goat.
Goat feeds man.
Class activity:
Let us make a food chain.
Hold hands to show who eats who.
Grass to goat to man.
Evaluation questions:
What does a plant make?
Who eats the grass?
What does the goat become?
Summary:
Food chains show how energy moves from plants to animals.

topics.title: Reuse and recycle
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sort recyclable materials.
The pupils should be able to reuse materials.
Introduction:
We have many used things at home.
We can use them again.
Content:
Reuse means using something again.
Recycle means making new things from old ones.
We can reuse bottles for water.
We can recycle paper to make new books.
We can recycle cans to make new things.
Class activity:
Let us sort our trash.
Put bottles in one box.
Put paper in another box.
Put cans in the last box.
We will make a bottle planter.
Evaluation questions:
What does reuse mean?
What can we recycle?
Show me a bottle we can reuse.
Summary:
Reusing and recycling helps our earth.

topics.title: Caring for the earth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to care for earth.
The pupils should be able to plant a tree.
Introduction:
The earth is our home.
We must take care of it.
Content:
We should not waste water.
Turn off taps when not using water.
We should not waste light.
Turn off lights when leaving a room.
We should plant trees.
Trees give us clean air.
Class activity:
Let us plant a class tree.
We will dig a small hole.
Put the tree in the hole.
Cover with soil and water it.
Evaluation questions:
Why should we save water?
What do trees give us?
Show how to turn off a tap.
Summary:
We must care for our earth by saving resources.

topics.title: Weather and seasons
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name two seasons.
The pupils should be able to dress for weather.
Introduction:
The weather changes every day.
Sometimes it rains, sometimes it is dry.
Content:
There are two main seasons in Nigeria.
Rainy season has lots of rain.
Dry season has no rain.
We dress for the weather.
In rainy season we wear raincoats.
In dry season we wear light clothes.
Class activity:
Let us dress for the weather.
When I say rain, put on imaginary raincoats.
When I say sun, put on hats.
Evaluation questions:
What season has rain?
What do we wear in the sun?
Show me how to walk in heavy rain.
Summary:
We dress differently for different weather.

topics.title: Day sky and night sky
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name day sky objects.
The pupils should be able to name night sky objects.
Introduction:
The sky looks different in day and night.
Let us learn about the sky.
Content:
In the day sky we see the sun.
The sun gives us light.
We also see clouds and rainbows.
In the night sky we see the moon.
The moon changes its shape.
We also see stars.
Class activity:
Let us draw the day sky.
Color the sun yellow.
Draw white clouds.
Now draw the night sky.
Color the moon gray.
Draw many stars.
Evaluation questions:
What do we see in the day sky?
What shape is the moon tonight?
Show me how the sun feels.
Summary:
The day and night sky have different objects.

topics.title: Revision and science fair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present a science project.
The pupils should be able to observe experiments.
Introduction:
We have learned many science things.
Let us share what we know.
Content:
Today we will have a science fair.
Each pupil will show their project.
You can show your plant cycle.
Or your bottle planter.
Or your habitat pictures.
Parents will come to see.
Class activity:
Let us set up our science fair.
Put projects on tables.
Practice explaining your project.
Evaluation questions:
What project did you make?
What did you learn this term?
Show your favorite science thing.
Summary:
We are all little scientists.
